III. Read the passage and answer the questions. (Questions 32–37)

Family time traditions are important in many countries. A recent study shows that such traditions are good for teens. They help young people feel closer to their parents and grandparents. They also make family life warmer and happier.

Some families have a tradition of eating dinner together at weekends. During the meal, parents and children talk about school, work and daily life. These fun conversations often lead to lots of laughter. Other families watch their favourite TV programmes together or play card games. These activities may look simple, but they can strengthen bonds with family.

In Viet Nam, many families have special traditions at Tet. They prepare offerings, worship ancestors and hold family reunions. Children wish their grandparents longevity, and adults give children lucky money. In addition to Tet, some families practise customs connected with local festivals, such as whale worship in coastal areas. Keeping these customs alive helps people remember their roots and respect their culture.

MINI REVIEW - ÔN TẬP NHANH BÀI HỌC

Từ vựng trọng tâm:
  • ancestor (n): ông bà, tổ tiên
  • offering (n): đồ cúng, lễ vật
  • longevity (n): sự sống lâu, trường thọ
  • strengthen (v): củng cố, thắt chặt
Cấu trúc ghi nhớ:
  • have a tradition of + V-ing: có truyền thống làm gì
  • instead of + V-ing: thay vì làm gì
  • It is + a + tradition for sb to V: đó là truyền thống để ai làm gì
  • Mạo từ: Không dùng "the" trước danh từ chỉ lễ hội (Tet, Halloween).
